definition: To re-explain the same context, constraints or preferences to a machine over and over, each fresh conversation rolling the boulder from the bottom of the hill.
etymology: From Sisyphus (the king condemned to eternal repetition) + phrase (Greek phrasis, ‘speech’); the seam falls on the shared s.
in_use: I spent the morning sisyphrasing the brand voice to it. Fourth time this week.
the_case: The mock-heroic register turns a daily tedium into a shared joke — which is how a word earns repetition of its own.
seo_title: sisyphrase — re-explaining yourself to AI in every new chat
seo_description: Every new chat, the same three paragraphs: who you are, the tone, the words to avoid. Sisyphrase names re-explaining yourself to a machine that never remembers.
